h1: Landscaping and garden care in Sidney
cardSummary: A compact seaside town of stratas, seniors’ residences and small lots, with a long list of protected tree species.
intro: Sidney is a compact seaside town: condo and apartment stratas, seniors’ residences, small single-family lots in West Sidney and Roberts Bay, and the shop frontages along Beacon Avenue.

The Town’s Tree Preservation Bylaw protects a long list of species, including seaside juniper and cascara alongside the usual natives, and any tree over 60 cm in diameter. A permit may be needed to remove, extensively prune or top a tree. See [grounds maintenance](/services/grounds-maintenance/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/?area=sidney).
localRulesIntro: Sidney protects a long list of species, and extensive pruning, not only removal, can need a permit. That matters for the big hedges and conifers around many stratas.

localNotes.title: Sidney Tree Preservation Bylaw
localNotes.text: Sidney's Tree Preservation Bylaw protects species including Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood, western yew, seaside juniper, cascara, shore pine, Douglas-fir, grand fir, western redcedar and bigleaf maple, plus replacement and permit-required trees, Town trees and any tree over 60 cm diameter. A permit may be needed to remove, extensively prune or top a tree on private property.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Salt and wind on the waterfront
conditions.body: Buildings along the Sidney waterfront and Roberts Bay take salt air and winter wind. Coastal-tolerant shrubs and grasses suit those edges.

conditions.title: Drier summers
conditions.body: Sidney tends to be on the drier side of the region in summer, so drip lines and mulch on beds go a long way, and lawns brown off quickly without them.

conditions.title: Shared grounds and residents
conditions.body: Most work here is on shared grounds used by residents every day. Clear paths, quiet hours and notes to council or management matter as much as the gardening.

topServices.why: Stratas and seniors’ residences need year-round care on a predictable schedule with clear reporting.
Hedges and conifers around buildings outgrow their space, and extensive pruning may need a permit first.

servicesBlurb.irrigation: Controllers set to the complex's street address for strata lawn days.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Hedge reductions and pruning with the Town's rules checked first.

jobNotes.title: Leaf-free paths for walkers
jobNotes.body: At a seniors’ residence, paths were cleared of leaf litter weekly through fall so walkers and wheelchairs had a safe surface.

jobNotes.title: Shopfront planters refreshed
jobNotes.body: Street-facing planters at a shopfront were replanted with low-water perennials and topped with mulch to get through the dry months.
